subject: Request: Bridging subsidy for HeliumHealth — capacity & latency remediation
messages:
From: Asha Rao <asha@heliumhealth.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: Jose Morales <jmorales@heliumhealth.com>, procurement@heliumhealth.com
Date: Sun, 10 Jun 2028 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Latency outage 2028-06-09 — request for remediation

Hi Tessa,

We saw a significant latency spike and partial gateway timeouts during the 09-Jun 02:00–05:30 UTC window. Our telemetry shows ~28% errors on our inference calls and tail latency jumped above 3s for conversational traffic. This caused multiple downstream retries and a visible UX degradation for several customers.

Can you confirm what happened and send a remediation proposal? Per our contract we expect availability and latency commitments; if there is a service shortfall we will need a commercial remedy (credits or other compensation) to cover the impacted period. Please point me to the postmortem and the proposed credit calculation.

Attaching a high-level slice of our request telemetry.

Thanks,
Asha Rao
Director of Product, HeliumHealth
--
HeliumHealth
attachments: request_slice.csv (csv)
From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: Asha Rao <asha@heliumhealth.com>
Cc: Jose Morales <jmorales@heliumhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jun 2028 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency outage 2028-06-09 — request for remediation

Hi Asha — thank you for the heads up and the telemetry. I’m really sorry HeliumHealth experienced that window. I’ve already engaged ops to produce a postmortem and we’ll run the usage/impact numbers.

What I’m proposing as immediate next steps:
- Ops sends a formal postmortem and the exact impacted request counts (ETA: EOD PDT tomorrow).
- I’ll draft a commercial bridging proposal for your review (credits / short-term subsidy) so you can present to procurement.
- If useful, we can schedule a quick sync this week to walk through the numbers.

I’ve attached the ops request for an initial diagnostics export and flagged this for sales leadership.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
attachments: ops_postmortem.pdf (stub)
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 10:17:00 -0700
Subject: Bridging subsidy proposal for HeliumHealth (requesting exec signoff)

Tessa / Marissa —

Thanks for flagging. Based on the initial ops numbers (errors + tail latency impact) and HeliumHealth’s expansion velocity, I recommend a targeted bridging subsidy that balances goodwill with margin control. Proposal:

Option A (preferred for speed): one-time account credit equal to 25% of June invoice (applied as billing credit).
Option B: a two-month subsidy where June is free (100% credit) and July at 50% of usage rate (billing discount).

Conditions:
- Attachments: ops_postmortem.pdf (ops), usage_window.csv (impact slice), proposed_credit_calc.xlsx (calc).
- Customer must sign an addendum acknowledging the remediation (no precedent language).
- Finance to confirm P&L impact; legal to confirm addendum language.

Please advise on an executive signoff or alternate band (I’m trying to avoid a multi-month unlimited credit).

lauren
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bridging subsidy proposal for HeliumHealth (requesting exec signoff)

Lauren — thanks for the clear options. A couple quick thoughts: HeliumHealth is in final contract negotiations for two additional product lines; preserving the relationship matters. I’d prefer a hybrid remedy: a modest one-time credit plus non-billing concessions (training hours, extended SRE on-call) instead of a full free month. That reduces revenue impact while providing tangible value.

Suggested counter: 20% one-time credit on June invoice + one month of onboarding/training credits (worth ~10k) + 60 days of elevated support (priority SRE routing). Finance, please confirm whether 20% is allowable against the committed ARR corridor.

-Marissa
VP, Customer Success & Sales
Redwood Inference

Team —

After weighing relationship impact and the finance signal: approve a hybrid remediation package for HeliumHealth on the following terms (one-time exception, non-precedent setting):

1) Commercial: 25% one-time credit applied to June 2028 invoice.
2) Support: 60 days of elevated SRE routing (priority queue) starting 15 Jun 2028.
3) Non-billing: two (2) onboarding/training credits (to be redeemed within 6 months).

Conditions:
- Customer must sign the addendum and acknowledge this is a one-off remedial package (legal to produce addendum).
- Finance to process a billing credit ticket referencing DEAL-4871 and mark as one-time write-down.
- This approval does NOT open any standing SLA concession policy; do not market this externally.

Tessa — please communicate the approved package to HeliumHealth and attach the addendum link. Once signed, Aditya, please queue the billing adjustment.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Chief Revenue Officer
Redwood Inference
